signature.name: Humble Administrator's Garden
signature.detail: The largest and most celebrated classical garden in Suzhou, a UNESCO-listed masterpiece of pavilions, ponds and borrowed scenery. Go early in the morning to beat the crowds, and book tickets online in advance during peak season.

signature.name: Suzhou Museum
signature.detail: A striking I. M. Pei-designed museum holding fine ceramics, calligraphy and local art, itself worth the visit for its architecture. Entry is free but timed reservations are required, so book ahead and avoid weekends.

signature.name: Tiger Hill, Suzhou
signature.detail: A historic park crowned by the leaning Yunyan Pagoda, with legends of a buried king and sweeping views. Allow a couple of hours to wander the gardens and climb to the pagoda.

signature.name: Tongli Water Town
signature.detail: A classic canal town of stone bridges, old lanes and boat rides just outside the city. Come on a weekday morning for quieter canals, and take a short boat ride to see it from the water.

signature.name: Pingjiang Road
signature.detail: A preserved old-town street along a canal, lined with teahouses, small shops and traditional houses. Visit in the late afternoon for softer light and fewer crowds, and try a canal-side teahouse.

signature.name: Hanshan Temple
signature.detail: A famous Buddhist temple tied to a beloved classical poem about its midnight bell. Dress modestly, keep quiet in the halls, and go early to enjoy the courtyards in peace.

signature.name: Lingering Garden
signature.detail: Another UNESCO-listed classical garden known for its intricate rockeries and elegant halls. Pair it with the Humble Administrator's Garden on a garden-focused day and buy a combined ticket if offered.

signature.name: Grand Canal Boat
signature.detail: A cruise along the historic Grand Canal shows Suzhou's water-town character from a different angle. Book a daytime or evening cruise in advance and bring a light layer for the breeze on deck.

transport: Metro about $0.50-1 a ride; taxis cheap
